steps.text: In a large bowl, combine zucchini, egg, and butter or margarine. Stir in seasoned crumbs, minced onion, and seasoning. Mix well.
Shape mixture into patties. Dredge in flour.
In a medium skillet, heat oil over medium high heat until hot. Fry patties in oil until golden brown on both sides.

raw_recipe.headline: Connie’s Zucchini “Crab” Cakes
raw_recipe.description: “These really taste like crab cakes but without the crab, and are a really good way to utilize that bumper crop of zucchini!”

review.reviewBody: Update: I made a double batch of these (to freeze for later use), and baked them on a lightly oiled baking sheet. 400 degree oven, turning once after 12 - 15 minutes then baking an additional 12-15 minutes. The results were great. Less oil absorbed than with pan frying, and the "crab" cakes came out crispy and golden, with a lot less mess and work. I've also made this with the commercial Italian Bread Crumbs. The flavor was out of this world! Outstanding! These make a wonderful vegetarian dinner when served with sliced tomatoes (topped with a dab of mayo) and fresh corn on the cob. These were so good that I make them at least once a week during the summer. I followed the suggestions of others, by lightly salting and draining the shredded zucchini before combining with the other ingrediants. The butter gives it a rich decadent taste!

I live in Maryland, and these definitely do not taste like a real crab cake, although they did remind me somewhat of the frozen grocery store kind. A reasonable facsimile for vegetarians. Due to previous complaints of sogginess, I squeezed the zucchini after grating it, and used commercial dried (canned) bread crumbs because they are denser than fresh bread crumbs (the recipe didn't specify which type to use). Also, "seasoned" bread crumbs were noted in the body, although seasoned was not specified in the ingredients list, which caused some confusion. As a Maryland crab cake afficionado, I would not recommend you use seasoned bread crumbs as the seasonings would detract from the Old Bay. I'll make these again, but next time I will increase the dried bread crumbs to 1 1/8 cups to help counteract the sogginess and increase the Old Bay to 1 1/2 tsp. to enhance the flavor.

A very good recipe. I have made these twice and the following changes work best for me-2 teaspoons Old Bay, 2 eggs instead of 1, 1/4 cup green onion chopped finely, fine bread crumbs so they pack into patties better, cover with crushed cracker, brush olive oil on both sides, and bake for about 30 mins at 400 deg...flipping once. We like them, and will make them again. (If the zucchini is coming from refrigeration, add 10 minutes to baking time.) We love these, and our home does not end up smelling like fried fish.

I took the advice of someone and increased the old bay to 1 & 1/2 tsp. and the bread crumbs to 1 & 1/8 cup....I've never ordered crab cakes as I think it's a waste of crab, but to me, the texture when making patties and the texture when eating probably resembles a crab cake...the recipe made 7 (3" to 4"patties). I fried them in coconut oil as I love the stuff....I'd guess about 3 minutes on each side til golden brown and crunchy....delicious...
 Make SURE you get as much liquid out of the zucchini as possible, otherwise they are too soft and don't get crispy....someone suggested a potato ricer and this worked great!

Yummy. Used 1 TBLS Old Bay...will use less next time. Used panko instead of flour, sprayed with canola oil on foil and grilled about 7 minutes per side. Turned out excellent. Made 6 patties. Served with a sauce of 1/2 c. Mayo, 1/3 cup roasted red peppers, 1 t. Cayanne. 1/2 cup breadcrumbs, no flour or panko. Cook in airfryer 20 minutes.

I really wanted this to come out like a less messy and time consuming version of breaded zucchini.
It didn't quite get there -- because I screwed up.
I wasn't paying enough attention to the directions and mixed the flour in with everything else.

It kept the patties from falling apart, but made them more bland. I didn't salt/drain the zucchinis (I had 2 smallish zucchini and 1 yellow summer squash, so I used all 3.)

TBH, I don't think I'd change much the next time. I'd add more Italian breadcrumbs and still add a bit of flour - just not as much as this first time. Add a bit more seasoning - always mindful of the sodium content in flavored crumbs - extra garlic and onion powders, maybe try some dried shallots. Whatever mood I'm in at the time, really.

I didn't fry them, but put parchment paper on a baking sheet, lightly spritz with coconut oil cooking spray (pump spray, not canned - the propellant can mess up the finish on cookware and appliances like waffle iron grids), formed/placed the patties and spritzed the tops. Baked them in a countertop oven for ~25 minutes at 375°. Sprinkled a bit of regular salt on them when I took them out - although, next time, I think I might use kosher salt instead of regular table salt.

I'm definitely going to keep making these. Tweaking the seasoning will make a big difference. I think I'll get more zucchini and summer squash this week and try again. See how my next batch goes.

Very good! I doubled the recipe, added diced red pepper, diced serranos, 4 garlic clove, and cilantro.
*Tip for people having trouble with zucchini moisture. Grate with thick cheese grater. Put a paper towel at the bottom of large bowl, then some crumpled parchement. Pour grated zucchini over. Cover and let sit in the fridge for 1-3 days. The zucchini will be light, fluffy, and so much easier to use!

An easy, tasty side. I grind and freeze fresh zucchini - which works perfectly for this recipe. When defrosted, most of the water separates and is easy to drain. As other reviewers suggested, I doubled the Old Bay, and dipped the patties in beaten egg, then cracker (or panko) crumbs. I gave ‘em a spritz of spray cooking oil and baked at 350 for about 30 minutes, turning halfway through. Turned out great!

Made exactly as directed. I used "hot" Old Bay and the seasoning was perfect. I tried the oven method (as recommended by another reviewer) but preferred the recipe exactly as written. UPDATE: Tried in the air fryer. Preheated to 350 degrees for 5 minutes. Froze the patties to maintain the shape for 5 to 10 minutes. Put parchment down. The first batch I tried to flip after 5 minutes but they were too crumbly. Cooked a total of 12 minutes. Crumbly. Second batch were frozen longer and I brushed olive oil on both sides. They held together better but I still prefer pan frying. I also prefer doubling the Old Bay and adding cayenne.

I’ve made this a few times and changed it up some. I made a batch last night and I made them into balls and rolled in bread crumbs, then flattened them out. I also fried them in butter - got a buttery crispy taste. I didn’t tell anyone they were zucchini until there was one left - everyone was shocked - they all thought crab cake. I put a tablespoon of old bay in it and I had about 11/2 lbs of shredded zucchini. Some one said it needed more old bay. Lol. Someone else said NO!! I also added 1/2 c shredded Parmesan

Marylander here! Nothing tastes like a crab cake, but an actual crab cake lol. These are a great little dish to make with all that leftover zucchini though. I grated the zucchini into a colander, and let it sit over a bowl. Mashed it with paper towels, and let it further drain for over an hour. The zucchini NEEDS to be as dry as possible. Added some finely chopped peppers and onions, not sure how much old bay I dumped in haha, added some roasted garlic and herb seasoning, black pepper - and added a dollop of mayo in addition to the egg. Basically added bread crumbs till the liquid/mix was absorbed. Fried in bacon grease on medium till both sides were golden brown.
Being allergic to seafood and living in Baltimore, this recipe is a lifesaver! My friends say it's very close to the "real thing".
I added baked striped bass , flaked Fantastic
I subbed almond flour for the bread crumbs. It worked perfectly and now they are lower carb, higher protein. They needed to cook for a bit longer. I also use a nonstick griddle and no oil.
It was great. I accidentally bought spicy Old Bay seasoning and it was just as good though a bit spicy for kids.
so delicious

This has to be the WORST recipe I've tried on this site! Unless you modify it eleventy different ways to reduce the moisture you will end up with a liquidy mess. There is no need for the melted butter. I'm now trying to figure out what to serve for dinner or if I should just put the whole blob in the oven and hope it comes out edible.

I've made this before but my review is missing - made these and baked them at 400 per other reviewer suggestion. I did add some garlic, dry mustard, parsley and dill in addition to the recipe. Were very good and I highly recommend you sweat the zucchini prior to mixing! - Aug 2022

Followed recipe without scanning reviews first. First of all, Recipe needs to be changed to instruct you to salt and drain the zucchini, squeezing out as much moisture as possible! Was very soggy and am sure that would improve the finished cake. Secondly, this tasted absolutely nothing like a crab cake! Zero! Thirdly, I went back and watched the video and they do NOT flour the patties but coated in crushed crackers which would certainly increase the crunch factor. Overall, as a veg side dish, if you remove moisture of zucchini first, should firm up better and be a nice squash patty. But as written, it was a soggy bland zucchini patty which had zero flavor of a crabcake. May try again with many modifications, as a squash patty to use up the abundant zucchini this time of year.

I am a big fan of zucchini but prefer fritters. I liked these but used crushed saltine cracker instead of the bread crumbs and left out the flour. I added a little chopped jalapeño for some more spice and they were delicious
